title: Combined past and future VISp inputs improved read-outs for one movie in ten Allen mice but left a gap
abstract: We tested time windows and activity gates in Allen natural movie three. We used 2,169 units from twelve mice. Two mice supplied development scores. We fixed the protocol before we scored ten validation mice. Each target had 20 units. Each primary source had 40 units. Source repeats and the two target halves were separate. Unit scales used only source repeats. Time validation had two-second guards. The combined VISp window covered one second before and after each target bin. It improved higher visual area (HVA) prediction in all ten validation mice. Mean noise-corrected explained variance rose from 0.0272 to 0.0439. The gain was 1.669 percentage points (95% mouse-bootstrap interval 1.356 to 1.989). The same window lowered VISp self-prediction by 3.546 points. Future-only input helped more than past-only input. This does not show causal integration. Other HVA sources kept a 3.545-point advantage with the same window (interval 1.880 to 5.009). Other HVAs exceeded VISp by 4.092 points with 60 current-bin units (interval 2.439 to 6.030). The difference was positive in nine mice. A 30/30 mixture was worse than 60 other-HVA units. A selected mean activity gate added 0.032 points beyond additive inputs (interval -0.043 to 0.117). Its median repeat correlation was 0.506. This noise weakens the null test of biological gain. These results describe observational read-outs with time windows. They do not explain the spectral hierarchy. Limits include one 120-second clip, sparse sources, weak absolute prediction, finite penalty grids and unmatched spatial coverage.

display.caption: Ten mice supplied protocol-validation scores. A window with past and future VISp bins improved HVA read-outs. It lowered VISp self-prediction. Grey points show mice. Colored points show means. Bars show 95% bootstrap intervals. Future inputs prevent a causal integration claim.
Each source had 60 units. Other higher visual areas predicted HVA responses better than VISp. A 30/30 mixture did not improve on 60 other-HVA units.
A fixed interaction block lowered prediction. Weight selection used 0, 0.1 and 1. It gave no clear gain over additive inputs. The mean activity gate had limited repeatability.
